title: Psalms Chapter 21 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 21 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 21 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 21.

questions.question: According to Psalms 21:1, in what does the king joy?
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:1 states that the king shall joy in the LORD's strength and greatly rejoice in His salvation.

questions.question: What has the LORD given the king according to Psalms 21:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:2 says that the LORD has given the king his heart's desire and has not withheld the request of his lips.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 21:3 says that the king wears a crown of silver.
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:3 states that God set a crown of pure gold on the king's head, not silver.

questions.question: What did the king ask for from the LORD according to Psalms 21:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:4 records that the king asked life of God and was given length of days forever and ever.

questions.question: According to Psalms 21:5, what has God laid upon the king?
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:5 states that God has laid honour and majesty upon the king.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 21:6 says the king is made exceeding glad with God's countenance.
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:6 clearly states that the king is made exceeding glad with God's countenance.

questions.question: In Psalms 21:7, in whom does the king trust?
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:7 states that the king trusteth in the LORD.

questions.question: According to Psalms 21:8, what shall the LORD's hand find out?
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:8 mentions that the LORD's hand shall find out all thine enemies.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 21:9 says the LORD will protect His enemies from His anger.
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:9 states that the LORD will swallow up His enemies in His wrath and the fire shall devour them, not protect them.

questions.question: What will happen to the fruit and seed of the enemies according to Psalms 21:10?
options: Destroyed from the earth and among men
questions.correctAnswer: Destroyed from the earth and among men
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:10 says that their fruit and seed shall be destroyed from the earth and among the children of men.

questions.question: What did the enemies intend against the LORD according to Psalms 21:11?
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:11 states that the enemies intended evil against the LORD and imagined a mischievous device.

questions.question: In Psalms 21:12, what will the LORD make the enemies do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:12 says the LORD shall make the enemies turn their back when He readies His arrows against them.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 21:13 calls for the LORD to be exalted in His own strength.
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:13 clearly states, 'Be thou exalted, LORD, in thine own strength.'

questions.question: Which comes first in Psalms 21: the king asking for life or God setting a crown on his head?
options: God setting a crown on his head
The king rejoicing in God's strength
questions.correctAnswer: God setting a crown on his head
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 21:3-4, God sets a crown on the king's head before the king asks for life.

questions.question: According to Psalms 21:5, the king's glory is great in what?
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:5 states that the king's glory is great in God's salvation.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 21 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 21 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 21:6, how has God made the king feel?
options: Most blessed forever and exceeding glad
questions.correctAnswer: Most blessed forever and exceeding glad
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:6 states that God made the king most blessed forever and exceeding glad with His countenance, showing divine favor and joy.

questions.question: What virtue is exemplified in Psalms 21:7 by the king’s attitude toward God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:7 explains that the king trusts in the LORD and will not be moved through the mercy of the Most High, emphasizing faith and reliance on God.

questions.question: What does Psalms 21:8 say God's hand will do?
options: Find out all enemies and those who hate Him
questions.correctAnswer: Find out all enemies and those who hate Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:8 clearly states that God's hand will find out all His enemies and His right hand will find those that hate Him, indicating divine justice.

questions.question: According to Psalms 21:9, what will happen to God's enemies in His anger?
options: They will be made as a fiery oven and devoured by fire
They will be banished to a distant land
They will be given a chance to repent
questions.correctAnswer: They will be made as a fiery oven and devoured by fire
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:9 describes God's wrath as causing His enemies to be like a fiery oven, swallowed up in His wrath and consumed by fire, reflecting judgment.

questions.question: What does Psalms 21:10 say about the fate of the enemies’ descendants?
options: Their fruit and seed will be destroyed from the earth
They will be protected by God
questions.correctAnswer: Their fruit and seed will be destroyed from the earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:10 states that the fruit and seed of the enemies will be destroyed from the earth and among the children of men, emphasizing the completeness of their defeat.

questions.question: How does Psalms 21:6–7 teach us about the relationship between God’s blessing and trust?
options: God blesses those who trust in Him and makes them glad forever
God blesses all people regardless of trust
Trust in God is irrelevant to receiving blessings
God only blesses kings who are wealthy
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses those who trust in Him and makes them glad forever
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 together show that God makes the king blessed forever and exceedingly glad (v.6) because the king trusts in the LORD and is firm through His mercy (v.7), connecting blessing with faith.

questions.question: What practical lesson about facing opposition can believers learn from Psalms 21:8–9?
options: God actively confronts and judges enemies who oppose Him and His people
Believers should seek revenge on their enemies
Opposition will always defeat the believer
Ignore enemies and hope they go away
questions.correctAnswer: God actively confronts and judges enemies who oppose Him and His people
questions.explanation: Verses 8 and 9 describe God’s hand finding His enemies and consuming them with fire in His anger, teaching that God defends and judges opposition rather than believers taking vengeance.

questions.question: A fellow believer is discouraged by enemies who plot evil. Based on Psalms 21:11–12, what biblical truth can you share?
options: Evil plans against God will fail and God will prepare to defeat enemies
Enemies will always succeed in their plans
God ignores the schemes of the wicked
Believers must fight their enemies physically
questions.correctAnswer: Evil plans against God will fail and God will prepare to defeat enemies
questions.explanation: Verses 11 and 12 reveal that enemies’ evil intentions will not succeed and God will turn them back by preparing His arrows against them, encouraging faith in divine protection.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 21:7, the king’s stability depends on his own strength rather than God's mercy.
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:7 clearly states that the king trusts in the LORD and through the mercy of the Most High he shall not be moved, showing that stability depends on God's mercy, not the king's own strength.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 21:13 encourages the LORD to be exalted in His strength and praises His power.
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:13 calls for the LORD to be exalted in His own strength and promises singing and praising His power, emphasizing worship and acknowledgment of divine might.

questions.question: What does Psalms 21:6–10 collectively teach about God’s response to blessing the king and opposing his enemies?
options: God blesses the king with joy and destroys the enemies completely
God ignores the king and protects the enemies
The king must fight his enemies alone
God blesses everyone equally without judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses the king with joy and destroys the enemies completely
questions.explanation: Verses 6–10 show God making the king blessed and glad, while finding and consuming enemies and destroying their descendants, illustrating both blessing for the faithful and judgment on foes.

questions.question: How does trusting in God's mercy, as described in Psalms 21:7, help a believer remain unshaken?
options: Because God's mercy provides unwavering support and protection
Because human strength is sufficient alone
Because enemies will always be absent
questions.correctAnswer: Because God's mercy provides unwavering support and protection
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:7 explains that the king trusts in the LORD and through the mercy of the Most High will not be moved, indicating that God's mercy sustains and stabilizes believers amidst challenges.

questions.question: According to Psalms 21:9–10, what is the extent of God's judgment on the enemies?
options: Their destruction is total, including their fruit and seed from the earth
They will be imprisoned but not destroyed
questions.correctAnswer: Their destruction is total, including their fruit and seed from the earth
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 10 describe the enemies being consumed by fire and their fruit and descendants destroyed from the earth, indicating complete judgment.

questions.question: What does Psalms 21:11 suggest about the power of human evil plans against God?
options: They are ultimately ineffective and cannot succeed
They cause God to change His mind
They bring temporary victory to the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: They are ultimately ineffective and cannot succeed
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:11 states that the evil devices imagined against God are not able to be performed, showing that human schemes against God fail.

questions.question: True or False: Based on Psalms 21:8–9, God’s power is shown through His protection of the king and destruction of his enemies.
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:8-9 shows God's hand finding enemies and His wrath devouring them, demonstrating His power in protecting the king and executing judgment.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 21 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 21.

questions.question: What device did the enemies imagine against the LORD that they were unable to perform?
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:11 states that the enemies 'imagined a mischievous device, which they are not able to perform,' highlighting their failed plans against God.

questions.question: According to Psalms 21:12, what will happen to the enemies when God makes ready His arrows?
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:12 explains that the enemies will 'make them turn their back' when God prepares His arrows against them, signaling their defeat.

questions.question: What is the main theme of Psalms 21:13?
options: Exalting the LORD in His strength
questions.correctAnswer: Exalting the LORD in His strength
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:13 calls to 'Be thou exalted, LORD, in thine own strength,' emphasizing praise and worship directed at God's power.

questions.question: The imagery of 'arrows upon thy strings' in Psalms 21:12 primarily symbolizes:
options: God's readiness to defeat His enemies
questions.correctAnswer: God's readiness to defeat His enemies
questions.explanation: The metaphor of 'arrows upon thy strings' in Psalms 21:12 depicts God's preparedness to strike down adversaries, a common ancient Near Eastern symbol of divine warfare.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God thwarting the plans of the wicked, similar to Psalms 21:11?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 21:30 states that 'There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the LORD,' echoing Psalms 21:11’s theme of the futility of wicked schemes against God.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 21:13 closes the chapter with a call to praise God for His mercy rather than His strength.
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:13 specifically calls to 'Be thou exalted, LORD, in thine own strength,' focusing on God's power, not mercy.

questions.question: In Psalms 21:11, what does the Hebrew word translated as 'device' (or 'mischievous device') imply about the enemies' plans?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term for 'device' (מַחֲשָׁבָה, machashabah) in Psalms 21:11 implies a secret, crafty, and harmful plan, emphasizing the covert and evil nature of the enemies' intentions.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of God defending His anointed one as seen in Psalms 21?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:30 refers to David as a forefather of Jesus, God's anointed king, reflecting the theme in Psalms 21 of God’s protection and blessing on His chosen king.

questions.question: How does the literary device of parallelism appear in Psalms 21:9?
options: By repeating the imagery of fire and destruction
By using chiasm to structure the verse
By alternating between first and second person
questions.correctAnswer: By repeating the imagery of fire and destruction
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:9 uses synonymous parallelism, repeating the imagery of fire consuming enemies to emphasize divine judgment and wrath.

questions.question: What is the significance of the enemies’ 'fruit' and 'seed' being destroyed as mentioned in Psalms 21:10?
options: It signifies the complete eradication of their lineage and influence
It means the loss of their wealth
It symbolizes their loss of freedom
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies the complete eradication of their lineage and influence
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:10 uses 'fruit' and 'seed' metaphorically to describe the total destruction of the enemies’ descendants and legacy, common in ancient Near Eastern texts.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 21 emphasizes that the king's confidence is in his own strength rather than in the LORD.
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:7 clearly states, 'For the king trusteth in the LORD,' showing the king’s confidence is placed in God’s mercy and strength, not his own.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage also uses the metaphor of God’s 'right hand' to describe His power against enemies, similar to Psalms 21:8?
questions.explanation: Exodus 15:6 describes the LORD's right hand as mighty in power, which parallels Psalms 21:8 where God’s right hand finds out His enemies, symbolizing divine strength.

questions.question: What is the historical-cultural significance of 'a fiery oven' in Psalms 21:9?
options: It represents an instrument of intense destruction familiar to ancient Near Eastern audiences
It symbolizes a place of worship
It refers to a cooking method for sacrifices
It is a metaphor for the sun
questions.correctAnswer: It represents an instrument of intense destruction familiar to ancient Near Eastern audiences
questions.explanation: The 'fiery oven' in Psalms 21:9 evokes images of intense heat and destruction, a vivid metaphor recognizable in the ancient Near East for God's consuming judgment against enemies.

questions.question: Which theme in Psalms 21 is a foreshadowing of the Messiah's victory as described in the New Testament?
options: God making the enemies turn their back and be defeated
The king wearing a crown of pure gold
The king's heart's desire being granted
questions.correctAnswer: God making the enemies turn their back and be defeated
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:12 foreshadows the Messiah's ultimate victory over evil, a theme fulfilled in the New Testament where Christ defeats spiritual enemies (cf. Colossians 2:15).

questions.question: How does Psalms 21 reflect the authorial intent to encourage the original audience?
options: By assuring them of God's protection over the king and His judgment on enemies
By instructing them to build a temple
questions.correctAnswer: By assuring them of God's protection over the king and His judgment on enemies
questions.explanation: The psalm, attributed to David, aims to encourage the original Israelite audience by affirming God's protection of their king and the inevitable defeat of his enemies (Psalms 21:7-13).

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 21 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 21 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 21 teach about God's response to the desires of the king?
questions.explanation: This is correct because Psalms 21:2 states that God has given the king his heart's desire and has not withheld the request of his lips.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated by His granting of long life to the king?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 21:4 shows God's mercy in granting the king life and length of days, reflecting His compassionate nature.

questions.question: According to Psalms 21, what is the king's response to God's strength?
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:1 indicates that the king shall joy in the strength of the Lord and greatly rejoice in His salvation.

questions.question: What metaphor is used in Psalms 21 to describe God's judgment on His enemies?
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:9 describes God's judgment on His enemies as making them like a fiery oven in His anger, illustrating the intensity of His wrath.

questions.question: Which verse demonstrates the idea that the king is blessed forever?
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:6 states that God has made the king most blessed forever, highlighting his enduring favor.

questions.question: What does Psalms 21:11 reveal about the intentions of the enemies of God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:11 clearly states that the enemies intended evil against God, showcasing their malicious intentions.

questions.question: How does the king's trust in the Lord influence his stability according to Psalms 21?
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:7 indicates that the king trusts in the Lord, and through the mercy of the Most High, he shall not be moved.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 3 and 5 convey about God's blessings?
questions.explanation: Verses 3 and 5 together illustrate that God blesses the king with goodness and also lays upon him honor and majesty, highlighting the richness of His blessings.

questions.question: What does Psalms 21:10 imply about the fate of the enemies of God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:10 indicates that God will destroy their fruit from the earth and their seed from among the children of men, showing their total eradication.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'Be thou exalted, LORD' in Psalms 21:13?
options: It is a call to worship
It is a command to the king
It is a declaration of defeat
questions.correctAnswer: It is a call to worship
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:13 is a call to exalt the Lord in His strength, indicating the appropriate response of worship and praise for His power.

questions.question: How does Psalms 21 reflect on the theme of divine sovereignty?
options: It affirms God's control over enemies
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms God's control over enemies
questions.explanation: The chapter repeatedly shows God's sovereignty, particularly in how He will deal with His enemies, as seen in verses 8-10.

questions.question: What does the term 'crown of pure gold' in Psalms 21:3 symbolize?
questions.explanation: The crown of pure gold symbolizes the authority and honor bestowed upon the king by God, as described in Psalms 21:3.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not care about the intentions of humanity. What does Psalms 21:11 teach?
options: God actively responds to evil intentions
questions.correctAnswer: God actively responds to evil intentions
questions.explanation: Psalms 21:11 teaches that God is aware of and actively responds to the evil intentions of humanity, demonstrating His engagement with the world.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 1 and 13 convey about the relationship between the king and God?
options: The king's joy is independent of God
The king rejoices in God's strength
The king does not acknowledge God
questions.correctAnswer: The king rejoices in God's strength
questions.explanation: Verses 1 and 13 together highlight the king's joy and praise in recognizing the strength and power of the Lord, showcasing a relationship of dependence and worship.

questions.question: How does the theme of salvation appear in this chapter?
questions.explanation: Psalms 21 highlights the theme of salvation as a source of great rejoicing for the king, especially in verses 1 and 5, which emphasize joy in God's saving power.
